Plot a fitted wisp model

plot.wisp.Rd

S3 method for plotting the results returned by wisp. This is the single public entry point for all wisp plotting: pick which plot to make with type, and pass that plot's own extra arguments through .... (This replaces the pre-2.6.0 API, where each plot had its own dotted, plot.*-named function that looked like an S3 method but never was, since wisp() results used to be plain, unclassed lists; see vignette("release_notes", package = "wispack") for the old-name to type mapping.)

Usage

# S3 method for class 'wisp'
plot(
  x,
  type,
  print.plots = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  species = "all",
  decompose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

List, output of the wisp function (an object of class "wisp").

type

Character string, which plot to make. One of:

  • "ratecount": plot the fitted model and observed data (counts) together for visual comparison, optionally with independent block boundaries. Set decompose = TRUE to instead plot the individual pieces of this plot, for a single species, separately. See the "ratecount" section below for its extra arguments.

  • "timeseries": plot timeseries effects, separated by a splitting factor (e.g., hemisphere). See the "timeseries" section below.

  • "parameters": violin (or bar) plots of the fitted wisp parameters, including confidence intervals if available. See the "parameters" section below.

  • "effect.dist": histograms of the fitted parameters. See the "effect.dist" section below.

  • "species.summary": rate-count, residual, and parameter plots for one species level, combined on one plot. See the "species.summary" section below.

  • "MCMC.walks": sampling of random walks and negative log likelihood from MCMC simulations. See the "MCMC.walks" section below.

  • "MCMC.bs.comparison": visually compare normality and autocorrelation of bootstrap and MCMC parameter estimates. See the "MCMC.bs.comparison" section below.

print.plots

Logical, defaults to TRUE. If TRUE, prints the plot(s) to the current graphics device as they are built; if FALSE, only returns them (without printing). Forwarded to every type except "species.summary", which has no print-control of its own and always prints its combined plot (see the "species.summary" section below).

verbose

Logical, defaults to TRUE. If TRUE, prints updates about the plotting process. Forwarded to every type.

species

Character vector, or the string "all" (the default), giving which species level(s) to include. "all" is translated internally to c(), this package's own "no filter, include everything" convention. Only forwarded to type %in% c("ratecount", "timeseries", "parameters", "species.summary"), since only those underlying plotting functions have a species argument; passing a non-default species for any other type raises a warning and is otherwise ignored. When decompose = TRUE, species must resolve to exactly one species level (i.e. not "all", and not a multi-element vector), or a clear error is raised.

decompose

Logical, defaults to FALSE. Only meaningful when type = "ratecount"; if TRUE, plots the individual pieces of the rate-count plot (data points only, fit lines only, and data points plus fit lines for individual random levels) for a single species separately, instead of the ordinary combined rate-count plot. This replaces the pre-2.6.0 type = "decomposition" (see vignette("release_notes", package = "wispack")). Setting decompose = TRUE for any other type is an error.

...

Additional arguments passed on to the plotting function selected by type; see the sections below for each type's own arguments.

Value

The return value depends on type; see the sections below. Most types return a list of ggplot objects, except type = "species.summary", which returns nothing (plots are printed to the current graphics device) and type = "MCMC.walks", which returns NULL early if the model has no MCMC sampling.

ratecount

Takes wisp model results (a fitted line) and observed data (counts) and plots them together for visual comparison. Can also include independent block boundaries for comparison if provided. With decompose = TRUE, instead returns the individual pieces of this plot (data points only, fit lines only, and data points plus fit lines for individual random levels) for a single species, plotted separately; species must then resolve to exactly one species level, or a clear error is raised.

  • log.scale Logical, if TRUE, plots rates and counts on a log scale; if FALSE, plots raw rates and counts.

  • CI_style Logical, if TRUE, plots predicted lines with confidence interval style shading; if FALSE, plots predicted lines as solid lines with random levels and data points. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

  • dim.boundaries Numeric vector, independent block boundaries to plot for comparison. If empty, the argument is ignored.

  • y.lim Numeric vector of length 2, limits for the y-axis of the plots. If NA (plain ratecount) or NULL (decompose = TRUE), defaults to automatic limits.

  • count.alpha.none Numeric, transparency for count points when random level is "none". If left NA, defaults to 0.25. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

  • count.alpha.ran Numeric, transparency for count points when random level is not "none". If left NA, defaults to 0.25. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

  • pred.alpha.none Numeric, transparency for predicted lines when random level is "none". If left NA, defaults to 1.0. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

  • pred.alpha.ran Numeric, transparency for predicted lines when random level is not "none". If left NA, defaults to 0.9. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

  • rans.to.print Character vector, list of random levels to include on each species plot. If c(), all random levels are included. Ignored when decompose = TRUE.

Returns a list of ggplot objects for rate-count plots (or, with decompose = TRUE, for the decomposed rate-count plots).

timeseries

Plots timeseries effects from wisp results, separated by a splitting factor (e.g., hemisphere).

  • splitting_factor Character string, the name of the fixed effect by which to split the timeseries. If empty, c(), the first non-timeseries fixed effect is used. If "none", will not split.

  • tertiary_effects Character vector, or NULL (default). Any fixed effects besides timeseries and the splitting factor are pruned down to a single level before rates are reconstructed (otherwise treatments belonging to different levels of those extra fixed effects would be mixed together). If NULL, each such fixed effect is pruned down to its reference level. Otherwise, for each additional fixed effect, if one of the levels named in tertiary_effects matches one of its levels, that level is used instead of the reference level.

  • log.scale Logical, if TRUE, plots rates and counts on a log scale; if FALSE, plots raw rates and counts.

Returns a list of ggplot objects for timeseries plots.

parameters

Makes nicely formatted violin (or bar) plots of the fitted wisp parameters, including confidence intervals if stat information is available.

  • violin Logical, if TRUE, plots violin plots for each parameter; if FALSE, uses bar plots.

  • species.classes List, a list of character vectors specifying which species levels to include together in plots. If NULL, all species levels are plotted separately.

  • mc_type Character string, type of model component to plot ("rate", "tpoint", "tslope"). If NULL, all model components are plotted.

Returns a list of ggplot objects for parameter plots.

effect.dist

Makes nicely formatted histograms of fitted parameters from wisp results. Has no species argument; species is ignored (with a warning) if set to a non-default value for this type. Returns a list of ggplot objects containing histograms of fitted parameters.

species.summary

Summarizes all important information (rate-count, residual, and parameter plots) for one or more individual species levels, each on one combined plot. Note that wisp() does not store built plot objects on its return value, so this always rebuilds the rate-count, residual, and parameter plots it needs fresh from x rather than reading them back from a stored $plots field. Unlike every other type, this one has no print.plots argument of its own and always prints its combined plots to the current graphics device; the dispatcher's print.plots argument has no effect here.

  • contexts Character vector, optional, specifies which context levels to summarize. Defaults to all.

Returns nothing; plots are printed to the current graphics device.

MCMC.walks

Makes nicely formatted plots of the random walks and (normalized) negative log likelihood sampled during MCMC simulation. Returns NULL early if the model has no MCMC sampling (i.e. x$sample.params.MCMC is empty/NULL). Has no species argument; species is ignored (with a warning) if set to a non-default value for this type.

  • low_samples Integer, number of low-value parameters to plot. Defaults to 10.

Returns a list of ggplot objects containing plots of walks for low-value parameters, high-value parameters, and normalized negative log likelihood (or NULL, see above).

MCMC.bs.comparison

Allows for visual comparison of the parameter estimates from bootstrapping vs MCMC simulation. Shows density for ten representative parameters from bootstrapping and MCMC walk, the distributions of Shapiro-Wilk p-values for bootstrapping vs MCMC walks, and the density of autocorrelation results for bootstrapping vs MCMC walks. Has no species argument; species is ignored (with a warning) if set to a non-default value for this type.

  • ran.seed Integer, random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to 1234. If NULL, no seed set.

Returns a list of ggplot objects containing plots of representative parameter distributions, Shapiro-Wilk normality test results, and autocorrelation plots for bootstrap and MCMC parameter estimates.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n_bins <- 20
bin <- sample(seq_len(n_bins), 400, replace = TRUE)
lambda <- rep(c(2, 8), each = n_bins / 2)
countdata <- data.frame(bin = bin, count = rpois(400, lambda[bin]))
model <- wisp(
  countdata,
  fit_only       = TRUE,
  model.settings = list(LRO_cost = "none"),
  plot.settings  = list(print.plots = FALSE),
  verbose        = FALSE
)
rc <- plot(model, type = "ratecount", print.plots = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
names(rc)
#> [1] "plot_pred_context_context_fixEff_species"
